note: Intent -> the path to take, the alternatives, and the one anchor to open. Hand-authored and gated by knowledge/tools/routing/check-routes.mjs. Prose stays in docs/: a route ends the choice, it does not restate the guide.

tasks.intent: Put two columns of content side by side on the page.
tasks.recommendedBecause: docs/recipes/layered-page-design.md#sidebar-page-background-vs-row states it directly: a column that holds content is a row column, because it flows and paginates with the main column.

alternatives.useWhen: the column is a tint that must repeat on every page and holds no content
alternatives.tradeoffs: costs nothing at layout time and never shifts content, but nothing can be placed in it — text in the sidebar still needs a row over the tint

alternatives.useWhen: the two columns are a data grid with a header row, not a page region
alternatives.tradeoffs: paginates per row and sizes columns by table rules rather than weights; a skills list in two columns is a row, not a table

alternatives.useWhen: the region is a fixed box needing pixel-precise (x, y) placement — a certificate or a badge
alternatives.tradeoffs: no flow and no pagination at all; the coordinates are yours to maintain

tasks.intent: Put a small icon to the left of a line or block of text.
tasks.recommendedBecause: docs/recipes/layered-page-design.md#icon-beside-text states the rule the signatures cannot: a row with no column spec, no grow spacer and the default START arrangement splits its inner width into equal shares, one per child, so a 13pt icon takes half the row. auto() is the icon's own width and weight(1) is everything left, which is the only form that stays right when the column is resized. RowWidthDistributionContractTest measures both, and the icon case on a real SvgIcon node.

alternatives.useWhen: a column of icons must line up down a list whatever each one contains
alternatives.tradeoffs: pins the rail exactly, but the point size now lives in the column spec as well as in the icon call, so the two can drift apart

alternatives.useWhen: both children are content and what you want is a proportion of the row — a 34/66 sidebar
alternatives.tradeoffs: a weight is a share, not a size: the ratio is chosen against one column width and is wrong at another, and it can hand a fixed-size icon a slot narrower than the icon itself

alternatives.useWhen: the row already needs its children pushed apart — a label left, a value hard right
alternatives.tradeoffs: a grow spacer switches the whole row to intrinsic sizing, which fixes the icon as a side effect but leaves no child able to take a proportional share, and it cannot be combined with columns() or weights() — the row rejects that pairing outright. A non-START arrangement(...) is the same switch by another name, so a row can land on this path without a spacer anywhere in it

alternatives.useWhen: the icon belongs inside the sentence rather than beside the block
alternatives.tradeoffs: there is no row and no width to distribute, but the icon wraps with the text line and cannot hold a fixed left rail for the paragraph to hang off

tasks.intent: Draw a rule or divider next to a heading, reaching the edge of the column.
tasks.recommendedBecause: docs/recipes/layered-page-design.md#a-rule-that-reaches-the-column-edge says what no signature can: horizontal(width) is points, not a percentage, and nothing clips a line to the space it was given. fill() stretches a horizontal line to its slot, and a weight column makes that slot the leftover width instead of half the row. Leave the heading unaligned — a right- or centre-aligned paragraph claims the whole row from the auto() column and the rule collapses to zero width. LineWidthUnitsContractTest measures the overflow, the repair and both ways the repair fails.

alternatives.useWhen: the rule is a fixed-length accent under a title, where the length is the design rather than a measurement of the column
alternatives.tradeoffs: the argument is points and nothing clips it, so a value guessed as a percentage is drawn at that many points straight across whatever is beside it, with no warning and a clean render

alternatives.useWhen: the rule is the last child and the heading beside it is short enough to survive an equal share
alternatives.tradeoffs: the rule does end on the row edge, but the even split still applies to the heading — it gets half the row and wraps, which is the same defect moved one child to the left

alternatives.useWhen: the heading has to be centred or right-aligned
alternatives.tradeoffs: the only form that survives an aligned heading, because the row decides the share instead of the text; the cost is that the heading no longer sizes to itself, so a short one leaves a gap before the rule rather than meeting it

tasks.intent: Decide which of the four placement tools a piece of page design needs.
tasks.recommendedBecause: docs/recipes/layered-page-design.md#the-four-tools presents flow as the default and the other three as the cases where flow is not enough.

alternatives.useWhen: the thing is a surface that repeats on every page and holds no content
alternatives.tradeoffs: free at layout time; cannot contain anything

alternatives.useWhen: elements genuinely overlap and the overlay should size itself to what it sits on
alternatives.tradeoffs: measures and sizes with its parent, so it stays correct when content changes

alternatives.useWhen: placement is pixel-precise inside a fixed box and must not reflow
alternatives.tradeoffs: no flow, no pagination, no measurement — coordinates are maintained by hand

tasks.intent: Keep a table's header row visible when the table runs past a page break.
tasks.recommendedBecause: docs/recipes/tables.md#repeated-header-on-page-break documents repeatHeader() for exactly this, and TableBuilderRepeatHeaderTest walks every page of a 60-row table asserting it.

alternatives.useWhen: each page's rows are a distinct group the reader should not read as one run
alternatives.tradeoffs: page breaks become content decisions and stop following the data; totals must be recomputed per part
